svg.text: Raise the Newton cutoff from 8 to 24 steps and ask what kind of slow geometry actually survives. Orange tiles still need at least 10 steps, or never settle by the cutoff.
What persists, and in what order

text.tspan: The hottest surviving center is still unity cubic z^3 - 1 at 77.0%.
The cleanest cooled center is asymmetric cubic at 0.0%.
The strongest near-critical retention is unity cubic z^3 - 1 at 86.6% of its old tail share.
The weakest retention is asymmetric cubic at 59.0%.
So the split-critical cubic really does land in a middle lane: less persistent than the unity singular core, much more persistent than the winner-take-most asymmetric cubic.
Dashed circle marks the unit circle; dashed crosshairs mark the origin. The useful difference is not just how much heat remains, but where it remains.
